{{Short description|Brewet sums are finite numbers introduced by brewer related to Jacobsthal sums}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Brewer sums''' are finite [[character sum]] introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Brewer|year1=1961|year2=1966}} related to [[Jacobsthal sum]]s.

==Definition==

The Brewer sum is given by
:<math>\Lambda_n(a) = \sum_{x\bmod p}\binom{D_{n+1}(x,a)}{p}</math>
where ''D''<sub>''n''</sub> is the [[Dickson polynomial]] (or "Brewer polynomial") given by 
:<math> D_{0}(x,a)=2,\quad D_1(x,a)=x,  \quad D_{n+1}(x,a)=xD_n(x,a)-aD_{n-1}(x,a)</math>
and () is the [[Legendre symbol]].

The Brewer sum is zero when ''n'' is [[coprime]] to ''q''<sup>2</sup>−1.
